title: Using function templates in multiple files
recap: Call sites normally need to see a template definition to instantiate it. A declaration alone in a header with the generic definition hidden in an unrelated source file is not enough.
Header guards prevent repeated inclusion in one translation unit; template definitions in headers can then be used consistently by multiple translation units.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice using function templates in multiple files.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement minOf<T>(left,right) in numeric.h, returning the smaller value (first on equality). Keep the full template definition visible in the header. main.cpp and the supplied probe.cpp both instantiate it; Alt+R through the provided CMake target builds both files. Do not edit the probe or put an int-only replacement in main.cpp.
hints: Put the whole generic minOf body in the header.
Compare the two T values and return the selected original value.
